profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 101 Aquila Way, Austell, GA, per mapping data. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's Atlanta metro property list did not surface a matching named/coded property at this specific address, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Atlanta metro footprint, with this specific site in Austell, a suburb west of downtown Atlanta along the I-20 corridor that has drawn substantial large-scale data center development in recent years, including major projects by other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. Georgia Power serves most of the metro Atlanta and Austell data center market. Digital Realty markets its Atlanta properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro within its global interconnection and colocation platform alongside its larger hub markets tracked elsewhere in this registry.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro market rather than per-building specifics for any US facility; this pattern of aggregate, not per-building, disclosure is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, and is not unique to this entry.

reading.body:
Digital Realty operates a facility in Austell, Georgia with a confirmed address but no published power capacity figure, making it impossible to assess its contribution to regional compute infrastructure from this data.

The facility sits within Digital Realty's Atlanta metro campus. Digital Realty itself is a publicly traded real estate investment trust that has grown through major acquisitions, including a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology in 2017 and an earlier purchase of AboveNet's East Coast operations in 2006. These transactions explain why some of the operator's facilities across multiple states still carry naming conventions from their previous owners.

The data confirms ATL11's street address and operator but does not include the power draw that would indicate whether this building is a significant regional load or a minor installation. The company has announced plans for a 10-story, 300,000 square foot expansion in Atlanta, but this data does not specify whether that project is underway, completed, or tied to ATL11 itself. Without capacity figures, the facility's actual relevance to Atlanta's power grid or to AI workload placement cannot be determined from this record.
